I have been farming in Quzhou for 30 years, and I know this land like the back of my hand. My 40 mu is mostly in wheat-maize rotation — that is what works here on the North China Plain, and that is what I have done for two decades. I keep 5 mu in cotton because the gin in the county still pays decent money for seed cotton, and my well can handle the water. I am 58 now and live alone, so I hire machinery for ploughing, sowing, and harvest, and I get local workers for peak times like cotton picking and spraying when both crops need attention.

For the winter wheat on my 35 mu, I will plant an improved variety — not the most expensive new hybrid, but the same one my neighbor Old Wang used last year and got over 500 jin per mu. I will put down 18 kg of nitrogen per mu total, half as base fertilizer and half topdressed at green-up and jointing. I know the bag says 15 kg is enough, but I would rather spend an extra 20 yuan per mu on urea than risk a thin stand. Phosphorus I do 6 kg per mu, potassium 4 kg. I irrigate three times: once in late March to wake the crop up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. My well water is steady. I spray pesticide twice, once for aphids and once for powdery mildew if it shows up. I rotary till before sowing in October. Last year I got about 550 kg per mu, and I expect the same if spring rain does not fail.

For summer maize on the same 35 mu, I plant a hybrid — everyone switched years ago, the traditional open-pollinated seed cannot touch hybrid yield. I apply 16 kg nitrogen per mu, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium. I irrigate twice, once at the big-flare stage and once at grain filling. After wheat harvest in early June there is no time to plough — the soil dries fast — so I no-till plant straight into the stubble. Two pesticide sprays, mainly for corn borer. I target 650 kg per mu; last year I hit 640, so 650 is reasonable.

For cotton on my 5 mu, I use an improved variety. Cotton is hungry for potassium, so I give it 13 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice and spray four times because bollworms will destroy you if you skip even one round. I rotary till in April before planting. I hire four or five women from the village to help pick in October. I expect about 300 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer prices have gone up again this year, and I thought about cutting back, but a bad harvest would cost me ten times more than an extra bag of compound fertilizer. I would rather waste 50 yuan on fertilizer than lose 500 yuan in grain. I watch what my neighbors do — if Old Wang and the Zhang family are putting down similar amounts, I know I am in the right range. That is my plan for this year.
